paragraphs: Project root for working with various forks and experiemnts for Micro LLM project. See .gitmodules for included repositories.

micro-llm is use-case agnostic: it holds the ESP32-S3 inference port, a generic tiny-model trainer, and pinned upstream sources. Domain tasks, data sources, and prompts live in consumer projects that import the trainer as a package; nothing here depends on a consumer. Sizes tagged est. are computed from published configs; claims not confirmed from a primary source are tagged unverified.

Sam is a very small Text-To-Speech (TTS) program written in C, that runs on most popular platforms. It is an adaption to C of the speech software SAM (Software Automatic Mouth) for the Commodore C64 published in the year 1982 by Don't Ask Software (now SoftVoice, Inc.). It includes a Text-To-Phoneme converter called reciter and a Phoneme-To-Speech routine for the final output. It is so small that it will work also on embedded computers. On my computer it takes less than 39KB (much smaller on embedded devices as the executable-overhead is not necessary) of disk space and is a fully stand alone…
